text: The Patriots got some good news and some bad news this week: on the bright side, Drake Maye put on a dominant performance in Sunday's 45-17 demolition of the Raiders, accounting for five touchdowns despite operating without his top receiver and with both starting cornerbacks sidelined, a display that suggests the young quarterback has found his confidence and his deep ball after a shaky start to the season. On the injury front, however, the team took some significant hits in that win, as running back TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain that's expected to sideline him for multiple weeks and left tackle Will Campbell sustained an MCL sprain in his right knee that will cost him some game action. The Patriots responded to the roster churn by signing RB Hassan Haskins and CB D'Shawn Jamison to the practice squad while releasing LB Jose Ramirez, and head coach Mike Vrabel addressed the week's developments in his Monday press conference. Meanwhile, off the field, Patriots legends Andre Tippett and Julian Edelman have been selected for induction into the International Jewish Sports Hall of Fame's Class of 2026, adding yet another honor to their already distinguished careers.
